newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil confirms lower IOF tax on foreign capital.
newsitem.headline: Brazil confirms lower IOF tax on foreign capital.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank confirmed it has cut a host of financial transaction taxes on foreign investment, including a lowering of its tariff on fixed income funds to two percent from seven percent.
In a statement, the Central Bank said the tax on all foreign loans to Brazilian borrowers, including Eurobonds and commercial paper, will be zero percent.
The tariff on non-resident transfers and interbank transactions in the foreign exchange market, both of which are carried out in so-called CC5 accounts, will be cut to two percent from seven percent.
The tax for investors in privatization bonds will be zero percent, while the IOF tax on Annex Four funds, used in stock market investments, will remain zero.
